summary: Ephemeral auth cookie rotation evicts tenant model pin during incremental canary surge
description: Issue summary: During an incremental canary for customer Veridian Health (dedicated), a short-lived auth cookie rotation correlated with a regional traffic surge caused a subset of their sessions to lose model pin affinity and be routed to the legacy fallback variant. Impact: Quality regressions for ~2% of requests for a 30-minute window; several customer API calls returned degraded completions causing user-visible errors in their triage UI. Environment: prod (us-west), dedicated pool r-verd-01. Observed behavior: sudden spike of fallback routing to gptx-13b-v1.4-legacy during a canary weight increase. Expected behavior: pinned sessions should retain affinity to the pinned model for the commit grace period and not be evicted by ephemeral cookie refreshes. Additional context: Customer reported this immediately after a scheduled canary weight change and a second-factor token refresh on their SSO that rotates the edge cookie.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer pins tenant to gptx-13b-v1.5-quant via tenant config and starts a staged canary (10% -> 30%).
2) Trigger tenant SSO re-auth flow which performs an auth cookie rotation (short TTL refresh).
3) Generate steady traffic (100rps) while increasing canary weight from 10% to 30% over ~10 minutes.
4) Observe a subset of existing sessions suddenly routed to fallback variant and model pin lost in routing logs.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: ephemeral auth cookie swap creates a transient mismatch between edge session identity and orchestrator's pinned-cohort mapping.
Reproduction: forcing cookie rotation during canary weight step reproduces ~2% silent fallback locally against a high-concurrency load generator.

Root cause: commit path race between orchestrator snapshot apply and edge-session rebind combined with prewarm mirror write ordering. When the edge presents a new cookie during the commit window, the session is treated as unpinned until the next snapshot reconciliation; prewarm mirror write sometimes writes a tombstone that blocks pin re-apply.
Scope: affects requests during short commit windows under concurrent cookie refreshes; more likely for customers using short-lived session cookies and high-throughput canary increases.
resolution: Workaround applied (customer set explicit model_name header for critical routes) which reduced user-facing regressions. Short-term mitigations deployed to edge to avoid header mutation during commit windows. Long-term fix: orchestrator PR #1123 adds a session-binding token check and changes prewarm mirror semantics to avoid tombstone overwrites; targeted rollout to prod-us-west on 2026-03-05 with canary verification. Postmortem and runbook update scheduled.
action_items: Deploy PR #1123 to prod-us-west with staged canary and extended telemetry for session-affinity metrics.
Update Canary Pinning Runbook to call out auth cookie rotation as a risk and recommend lengthening pin grace period for short-lived cookies.
Follow up with Veridian Health to validate fix and revert temporary explicit model_name header after verification.
Add synthetic test covering cookie rotation during weight changes to CI canary tests.
